uten_bank.tekst:
Nephrocalcinosis er en vanlig produksjonslidelse hos oppdrettslaks, særlig under smoltproduksjon, med prevalens som varierer fra mild til alvorlig på tvers av norske oppdrettsanlegg og er sjelden i villfiskpopulasjoner. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/169309659] Mineralavleiringer består hovedsakelig av amorft kalsiumfosfat (amCAP) i nyrene, og i alvorlige tilfeller kan nesten hele nyrestrukturen gå tapt. [#10.1016/j.aquaculture.2022.738104] Plasmaanalyse viser lave klorid- og natriumnivåer, samtidig med forhøyede kalsium‑ og magnesiumkonsentrasjoner, endret glukosenivå, nedregulering av Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase‑subenheter (NKAα1b1, -b2, -c1, -c2) og redusert uttrykk for sulfatransportere (SLC26a1a, -1b, SLC26a6a1) i takt med økende nephrocalcinosis‑grad. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/295422684] Magnesiumtransportere viser varierende respons; noen er oppregulert mens andre forblir uendret eller nedregulert avhengig av alvorlighetsgrad. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/295422684] Osmoregulatorisk stress forårsaket av mismatched salinitetsignaler under smoltifikasjon fører til kronisk hyperkalsiemi og hypermagnesiemi, som kan oversaturere urinen og føre til kalsiumavleiringer i nyrene. [#10.1111/jfd.13815] Økte CO₂‑partialtrykk i oppdrettsvann øker forekomsten av nephrocalcinosis; fisk eksponert for 8–11 mmHg CO₂ hadde 34 % prevalens versus ingen tilfeller ved kontrollnivåer. [#10.1016/j.aquaculture.2017.09.012] Transkriptomisk profilering av alvorlig påvirket lakse viser massiv nedregulering av metabolske og energiproduksjons‑gener, oppregulering av vevsreparasjonssignaler og forsterkede inflammatoriske responser. [#10.1111/jfd.13687] Radiografisk bildebehandling kan påvise nephrocalcinosis hos oppdrettslaks. [#10.1111/jfd.13704] Nephrocalcinosis er en ledende dødelighetsfaktor før havoverføring, ofte i samspill med hemorragisk smolt‑syndrom. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/169309659]

uten_bank.tekst:
Disease and stress are major welfare challenges in Atlantic salmon aquaculture, with welfare indicators guiding assessment. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/98698871]  
Salinity changes during smoltification create osmotic stress that has been linked to nephrocalcinosis in juvenile Atlantic salmon. [#10.1111/jfd.13815]  
The mismatch between salinity and day‑length signals increases the risk of kidney calcification by causing chronic hypercalcaemia and hypermagnesaemia. [#10.1111/jfd.13815]  
Nephrocalcinosis is associated with altered plasma ion concentrations, reduced Na⁺/K⁺ pump expression, and changes in magnesium transporter genes. [#https://core.ac.uk/works/295422684]  
Urocystolithiasis, an underdiagnosed bladder mineralisation, can obstruct the urinary tract and compromise welfare in farmed Atlantic salmon. [#10.1111/jfd.70099]  
Harmful algal blooms cause acute mortality, appetite loss, and behavioural changes before death in sea‑cage salmon. [#10.1111/jfd.70162]  
Amoebic gill disease lesions are detected by computer vision, which shows a positive association between ventilation rates and gross gill score. [#10.1111/jfd.70055]  
Environmental DNA and RNA monitoring in recirculating aquaculture systems provides non‑lethal early detection of key viral and bacterial pathogens. [#10.1016/j.aquaculture.2025.743060]  
Ultrasound, a technique used in human medicine, reliably semi‑quantifies gas bubbles and predicts acute gas bubble disease risk in Atlantic salmon. [#10.1111/jfd.14142]  
Vaccination against pancreas disease with DNA or inactivated SAV vaccines increases weight gain and reduces mortality during SAV2 outbreaks. [#10.1111/jfd.70003]  
Gradual acclimatization to low seawater salinity before sea transfer decreases Tenacibaculum finnmarkense infection severity and mortality. [#https://europepmc.org/article/AGR/IND609372435]  
Stunted salmon exhibit incomplete smoltification, evidenced by lower Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase subunit expression, reduced thyroid hormones, and similar cortisol levels. [#10.1016/j.aquaculture.2023.740078]

The Norwegian guideline for rainbow trout welfare explicitly lists anesthesia/euthanasia and slaughter as key procedures to be monitored with operative and environmental indicators, underscoring their importance in welfare assessment [#https://core.ac.uk/works/98698871].  
During the transition from freshwater to seawater, Atlantic salmon undergo a complex smoltification process that involves dramatic endocrine shifts; fish that have not fully adapted exhibit lower plasma thyroid hormones (T4, T3) and growth hormone, which are associated with higher mortality and disease susceptibility after transfer [#https://europepmc.org/article/AGR/IND609250302].
